summary: Final neuronal RNA-seq NGS reanalysis readout for Doventhar Therapeutics. Junction-level analysis resolved the apparent gene-expression conflict and supported a focused validation experiment; the deck preserves annotation provenance and the limits of computational inference.

properties.title: QV.15.065 neuronal splice-junction reanalysis v2
properties.subject: NGS reanalysis and focused validation design

slides.title: Neuronal RNA-seq: splice-junction reanalysis
slides.subtitle:
{{PRJ0076:project_id}} | Doventhar Therapeutics | 23 Dec 2015
Dr T. Zawiernicki | Quenverell Computational Ltd

slides.title: Question and model-gate outcome
bullets: Can junction-level evidence explain the apparent gene-expression conflict?
NGS reanalysis resolved the apparent conflict at junction level.
The result supports a focused validation experiment.
The computational interpretation is not experimental validation.

slides.title: Engagement chronology
bullets: Start: 05 Oct 2015; interim discussion: 13 Nov 2015.
Final reanalysis readout: 23 Dec 2015.
Data provenance accession: {{PRJ0076:lims_id}}.

slides.title: Source evidence
bullets: Doventhar Therapeutics supplied neuronal RNA-seq for reanalysis.
Retain read-level inputs and sample annotations together.
Link derived junction evidence back to the original sample identifiers.

slides.title: The apparent conflict
bullets: Gene-level summaries did not provide a coherent biological interpretation.
A gene-level total aggregates reads from different transcript configurations.
Investigate the junction evidence before treating the discrepancy as a contradictory biological response.

slides.title: Data acceptance
bullets: Check sample mapping and read-level input integrity.
Review alignment ambiguity and junction-supporting reads.
Keep failed acceptance checks distinct from absence of biological evidence.

slides.title: Annotation reconciliation
bullets: Keep reference sequence and transcript annotation versions explicit.
Map junction coordinates consistently before comparing samples.
Do not silently combine counts generated from different annotation definitions.

slides.title: Junction-level analysis route
bullets: Recover splice-spanning evidence from the accepted RNA-seq input.
Associate junctions with compatible transcript configurations.
Compare the relevant junction patterns with the gene-level interpretation.

slides.title: What a junction measures
bullets: A splice-spanning read supports a connection between exonic regions.
Support for a connection does not by itself establish a complete transcript.
Read depth and mapping ambiguity affect confidence in interpretation.

slides.title: Comparison with gene-level totals
bullets: Preserve gene-level summaries as a contextual measure.
Ask whether the aggregated expression total masks distinct transcript usage.
Do not equate changed junction representation with changed total expression.

slides.title: Resolved interpretation
bullets: Junction-level analysis resolved the apparent gene-expression conflict.
The interpretation should therefore refer to the informative junctions.
Avoid carrying the original conflict forward as evidence for opposing mechanisms.

slides.title: Evidence boundaries
bullets: No numerical junction table is supplied in this readout.
No specific transcript identifier is assigned here without the source annotation.
The qualitative outcome supports experimental focus, rather than a quantitative effect claim.

slides.title: Model uncertainty
bullets: Ambiguously aligned reads can support more than one explanation.
Transcript annotation incompleteness limits reconstruction.
Neuronal sample composition can influence aggregate expression.

slides.title: Focused validation question
bullets: Does an independent measurement support the junction interpretation?
Select an assay that distinguishes the informative splice connection from shared transcript sequence.
Retain a gene-level measurement as context rather than the sole endpoint.

slides.title: Proposed validation design
bullets: Use junction-spanning primers where the sequence permits.
Include a shared-region assay and appropriate negative controls.
Assess specificity before interpreting biological samples.
Use matched material where available and preserve sample provenance.

slides.title: Decision criteria for follow-up
bullets: Concordant junction evidence supports the reanalysis interpretation.
Discordance requires review of assay specificity, mapping and sample identity.
Do not resolve discordance by changing transcript labels after seeing the result.

slides.title: Reproducibility responsibilities
bullets: Dr E. Ostlund: junction-level interpretation.
Nadia Rahmani: input mapping and annotation provenance.
Dr T. Zawiernicki: final model-gate recommendation.

slides.title: Analysis notebook handover
bullets: Retain input identifiers, alignment settings and annotation versions under {{PRJ0076:lims_id}}.
Preserve junction definitions and their connection to gene summaries.
Keep the interim conflict and final resolution dated and traceable.

slides.title: Final recommendation
bullets: Close {{PRJ0076:project_id}} with the junction-level interpretation.
Proceed to a focused validation experiment.
Report computational resolution separately from experimental confirmation.
Dr T. Zawiernicki | 23 Dec 2015
